{{Short description|Chinese-American solid-state physicist}}
'''Frank F. Fang''' (born 11 September 1930) is a Chinese-American solid-state physicist. Born in [[Beijing]], he was part of the team that succeeded in 1966 in the detection of a [[two-dimensional electron gas]] and its quantum properties in [[semiconductor]]s.

== Education and career ==
Fang studied at the [[National Taiwan University]] with a bachelor's degree in 1951 and the [[University of Notre Dame]] with a master's degree in 1954. In 1959 he received his doctorate in electrical engineering at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. In 1959/60 he worked for [[Boeing]] and from 1960 he did research at [[International Business Machines | IBM]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://history.aip.org/phn/11508019.html | title = Frank F. Fang. Biography | website = Physics History Network | publisher = AIP }}</ref>

[[John Robert Schrieffer]] had predicted 1956 quantum effects in electron transport due to the two-dimensional geometry in metal-insulator-semiconductor structure (MIS). The detection was first successfully achieved by the team of Fang, [[Alan B. Fowler]], [[Phillip J. Stiles]] and [[Webster Eugene Howard]] at IBM in 1966 by applying strong magnetic fields.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Fowler, AB|author2= Fang, FF|author3=Howard, WE|author4=Stiles PJ| title = Magneto-Oscillatory Conductance in Silicon Surfaces | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 16 | number = 20 | date = 16 May 1966 | pages = 901–903 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.16.901|bibcode= 1966PhRvL..16..901F}} </ref>

In 1982 Fang was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. In 1984 he was elected an [[IEEE]] Fellow for "the discovery and explanation of two-dimensional properties of silicon inversion layers and for contributions to semiconductor device research."<ref> [https://www.ieee.org/membership/fellows/fellows-directory.html IEEE Fellows Directory] (''Citation: For discovery and understanding of the two-dimensional properties of silicon inversion layers and for contributions to semiconductor device physics research.'')</ref>

In 1981, he received the [[John Price Wetherill Medal|Wetherill Medal]] from the [[Franklin Institute]] with Fowler, Howard, Stiles and [[Frank Stern (physicist) | Frank Stern]]; Stern and Howard gave the theoretical explanation of the 1966 experiment.<ref> {{cite journal | author = Stern, Frank|author2= Howard, WE | title = Properties of Semiconductor Surface Inversion Layers in the Electric Quantum Limit | journal = Physical Review | volume = 163 | number = 3 | date = 15 November 1967 | pages = 816–835 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRev.163.816|bibcode= 1967PhRv..163..816S }}</ref> In 1988 Fang received with Alan B. Fowler and Phillip J. Stiles the [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize]].
